items.title: Mitra Tamil empowerment programme: RM900k allocation benefits 8,690 SPM, STPM students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 8,690 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) candidates nationwide have benefited from the 2026 Tamil Language Excellence Empowerment Programme, involving an allocation of RM901,680. The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), under the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma), said the programme was implemented in collaboration with the Education Ministry (MOE) to improve academic performance and Tamil language proficiency. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said 7,897 SPM candidates and 793 STPM candidates who sat for the Tamil Language paper nationwide had benefited from the programme.

items.title: KTMB records 7 railway trespassing cases in nine months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) recorded seven cases of people trespassing on railway tracks between January and September this year, disrupting train services. In the latest incident, an SUV entered the tracks at Port Klang Station on Sunday, causing delays to train services. KTMB said the vehicle entered the tracks through a level crossing gate.

items.title: Yeo proposes Langkawi or Penang as Disney cruise hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should negotiate with Disney Cruise Line to make Langkawi or Penang a departure and arrival hub for its Disney Adventure cruise ship, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong) said Malaysia should aim to become more than just a port of call by allowing international tourists to begin or end their cruises at either destination. Yeo said the arrangement could encourage tourists to spend several days in Malaysia before or after their cruise, benefiting the local tourism industry.

items.title: United Malacca's executive director Lip Sin passes away
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: United Malacca Bhd has announced that its executive director Datuk Seri Tee Lip Sin has passed away at the age of 55. He was the group managing director of Prosper Group and a director of Prosper Capital Holdings, a substantial shareholder of United Malacca. Tee held 1.98 million United Malacca shares directly and 179,700 shares indirectly, through his spouse and children.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1555611]] [[nid:1555610]] [[nid:1555609]] [[nid:1555608]] [[nid:1555607]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: IMF chief urges urgent fiscal action as global economic resilience reaches limits
items.summary: ISTANBUL: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva on Wednesday urged governments to urgently strengthen public finances, warning that the global economy's resilience to repeated shocks is reaching its limits, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Speaking at a press briefing during the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Georgieva said energy and fiscal buffers were being depleted, while persistent inflation and rising interest rates were adding to debt-servicing pressures. Georgieva said government bond yields in advanced economies had risen to multidecade highs, reflecting inflation, investment demand, expectations of stronger AI-driven growth and fiscal weaknesses.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 14, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Malaysians remain safe Malaysians in Riyadh remain safe despite recent security incidents, with the government closely monitoring the situation through daily reports from its missions in Saudi Arabia. Nazir returns to MACC Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin was summoned to the MACC headquarters over a notice requiring him to declare his assets. Joint haze measures Malaysia and Indonesia have begun discussions on joint efforts to address forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that have contributed to transboundary haze.

items.title: Infomina's net profit rose 30.6pct in Q1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd's net profit rose 30.6 per cent to RM10.55 million in the first quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM8.08 million a year ago. The increase was mainly due to higher profit contribution from the technology infrastructure operations, maintenance and support services segment, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. Quarterly revenue rose 39.5 per cent to RM76.19 million from RM54.63 million previously, driven by higher revenue contribution from the same segment.

items.title: FBM KLCI expansion to better reflect Malaysia's economy, stock weighting impact manageable – AHAM Capital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents is expected to provide a more accurate representation of Malaysia's domestic economy. The impact on the weightings of existing constituents is expected to be manageable, according to AHAM Asset Management Bhd (AHAM Capital). The implementation will take place from Dec 21, 2026, with Phase 1 seeing 20 new constituents added to the FBM KLCI at 50 per cent of their final index weight.

items.title: Penang's RM114.8mil Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project 50.86pct complete
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang's RM114.8 million Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project is 50.86 per cent complete, with full completion scheduled for Sept 20, 2027. State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the project aimed to reduce flash flood risks across the 51sq km Sungai Pinang river basin, where rapid development had placed increasing pressure on existing drainage infrastructure. "The project is expected to reduce the flood-affected area in parts of the Sungai Pinang basin by 10.15 per cent, while reducing damage to public infrastructure, residents' properties, housing and transport links," he said during a visit to Phase One of the Sungai Pinang river basin flood mitigation plan.

items.title: Haze: Education Ministry coordinating school operating procedures under new action plan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) to ensure that decisions on school closures are made in a more systematic manner, taking into account Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and health advice. Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said that under the coordinated procedures, outdoor activities would be postponed when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed when the reading exceeds 200, in accordance with the PTJK. “Closing schools several days in advance without taking these changes into account could result in children losing learning time even after air quality has returned to normal,” she said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: PM Anwar extends donation to Makkal Osai senior editor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 (Bernama) — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended a donation to Makkal Osai senior editor Rajan Boopalan, who is undergoing treatment at Selayang Hospital after suffering a blood clot in his head. Anwar said several officers from the Prime Minister’s Office had visited Rajan at the hospital on his behalf. He also prayed for Rajan’s speedy recovery and for his treatment to proceed smoothly.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Royal succession disputes must follow adat, law
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests. Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state's stability. The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin.

items.title: Malay Rulers urge outsiders not to politicise Negeri Sembilan throne dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —The Malay Rulers have urged outsiders not to interfere in or politicise the dispute over the Negeri Sembilan throne, calling for the matter to be resolved by the relevant authorities through proper legal and customary channels. In a statement issued today by Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad on behalf of the Malay Rulers, all parties involved were urged to exercise wisdom, patience and respect for adab, adat and the dignity of the royal institution. As efforts to resolve the dispute continue, the Malay Rulers urged all parties to preserve family ties, social harmony and respect for the royal institution while avoiding statements or actions that could aggravate tensions.

items.title: Don't politicise Negri Sembilan crisis, say Malay rulers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malay Rulers have warned against outside interference and attempts to politicise the Negri Sembilan royal crisis, saying the dispute must be resolved through lawful channels by the relevant authorities. In a statement issued today, the Malay Rulers said the issue must not be exploited for political gain, to garner public support or to expand influence in pursuit of power. The statement was issued by Keeper of the Rulers' Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad in accordance with the royal decree of the Malay Rulers.

items.title: 5 men sought over Semenyih murder
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police are hunting five men believed to be involved in the murder of a local man whose body was found buried in Semenyih, Kajang. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said 15 suspects, including two foreigners, had been arrested, with several already charged in court. Shazeli said the suspects, aged between 35 and 48, were believed to be in Selangor.

items.title: 'It takes a nation to raise a child': MP calls for joint action on school safety
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Concerns over nihilistic violent extremism (NVE) among schoolchildren require joint action by the government, schools and parents, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) said the ideology was believed to have spread among pupils, raising concerns that they could be drawn into violence. Mas Ermieyati said teachers needed adequate support to identify pupils experiencing emotional distress, learning difficulties or food insecurity while managing their classes.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Royal succession disputes must follow adat, law
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Oct 14 — Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests, Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said today. His Royal Highness stressed that the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state’s stability. The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.

items.title: Oil prices surge as Iran deploys new tactics to target tankers
items.summary: LONDON: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, while Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence US midterm elections. Brent crude futures rose 91 cents, or 0.9 per cent, to US$106.60 a barrel at 1110 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose US$1.65, or 1.8 per cent, to US$95.79 a barrel, its highest in more than two weeks.

items.title: Couple jailed up to 8 years over man's death in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The High Court here today sentenced a couple to seven and eight years in prison for causing a man's death by negligence in Kampung Gondang, Ketereh, four years ago. Judge Datuk Azhar Mokhtar sentenced Maizatul Shima Abdullah, 25, to eight years' imprisonment, while Muhammad Za'im Syakir Sha'ari, 24, was jailed for seven years. The court also ordered both accused to pay RM2,500 each in compensation to the victim's family under Section 425A of the Criminal Procedure Code.

items.title: Ringgit closes higher against US dollar on improved risk appetite
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the greenback on Wednesday as investors' risk appetite improved ahead of US inflation data, with sentiment supported by the 2027 Budget announcement last week. At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0805/0850 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment appeared to be focused on the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data due later tonight.

items.title: Nazir Hussin spends 2 hours at MACC over asset declaration notice
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin spent about two hours at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters. Nazir was called in to receive a notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009, which requires individuals to declare their assets. On Oct 1, the MACC remanded two corporate figures, brothers in their 40s and 50s who hold the titles Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira, for five days to assist investigations into alleged collusion and abuse of power involving an investment worth about RM10 million.

items.title: JAG to acquire a freehold land in Shah Alam to expand waste management business
items.summary: In a statement, the group said the acquisition was part of its proposed expansion of its total waste management business, which requires a total capital investment of about RM60 million, including land and equipment. JAG said the expansion would involve establishing new production lines and increasing storage capacity to strengthen its processing capabilities and operational flexibility. The expansion would enhance the group's ability to recover valuable materials from these waste streams through its existing recycling and resource recovery capabilities.

items.title: Stroke survivor faces RM91,657 bill over Bitcoin mining
items.summary: KUANTAN: A stroke survivor is facing a RM91,657 compound after her house in Cherating was allegedly used for illegal Bitcoin mining, leaving the property damaged. Rabiatul Adawiyah Abdul Rahman, 35, said she had no reason to suspect wrongdoing as her monthly electricity bills ranged from RM6 to RM30 and her rent was paid promptly. Rabiatul suffered a stroke on May 12, which prevented her from visiting the property.

items.title: Judgment reserved in Saifuddin Nasution’s appeal over RM600,000 awarded to Sanusi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Court of Appeal today reserved its judgment in Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s appeal against the Alor Setar High Court decision ordering him to pay RM600,000 in damages to Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor for defamation. A three-member bench led by Judge Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli deferred its decision after hearing submissions from Saifuddin Nasution’s counsel Razlan Hadri Zulkifli and counsel Yusfarizal Yussoff, who represented Muhammad Sanusi. On Aug 24, 2025, the Alor Setar High Court allowed Muhammad Sanusi’s suit against Saifuddin Nasution after finding the latter liable for defamation.

items.title: Creative content drive must be matched by child online safety measures, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Efforts to promote creative content on digital platforms must go hand in hand with measures to protect children from online sexual crimes, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. “We want to encourage the production of creative content, including on platforms such as YouTube. Fahmi said the Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continued to encourage creative content production, including on digital platforms, as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s creative economy.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan JPJ impounds four luxury cars driven by unlicensed foreigners
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 14 —The Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized four luxury vehicles driven by non-citizens under Op Luxury PeWA, an operation targeting foreign drivers who violate road transport laws. State JPJ director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said the vehicles comprised a Toyota Vellfire, two Mercedes-Benz A250s and a BMW limousine, driven by Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Chinese and Myanmar nationals aged between 30 and 40. Of the vehicles seized, 313 were motorcycles, 149 were cars and 36 were goods vehicles.

items.title: Perlis power plant project requires funding commitment of up to RM479.4mil to Kinergy Advancement's unit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The maximum funding commitment for the development of the Eentier Perlis power plant to KAB Energy Holdings Sdn Bhd (KABEH), the wholly owned subsidiary of Kinergy Advancement Bhd (KAB), is RM479.4 million. This being the 51 per cent of the total equity portion of the project of RM940 million, said KAB in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. The total project cost for the Phase 1 of the Perlis power plan stands at RM4.7 billion.

items.title: Police arrest 29 men over alleged spread of banned groups’ propaganda on social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Police have arrested 29 men, including a foreigner, on suspicion of promoting and spreading propaganda related to illegal organisations on social media. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects, aged 18 to 49, were arrested under Ops Mega TikTok 2026, conducted from Oct 10-12. “As a result of the operation, involving 11 police contingents in Selangor, Johor, Pahang, Penang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Kedah, Melaka, Sabah and Sarawak, 28 Malaysians and a foreigner were arrested,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: No police reports lodged alleging Zara Qairina was murdered, court told
items.summary: Wong: Correct. Wong: Correct. Wong: Correct.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 14, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher for a third consecutive session, supported by bargain hunting following last week's sell-off and 2027 Budget announcement. The benchmark index increased 4.37 points to 1,627.72. Meanwhile, the ringgit closed higher against the US dollar to 4.0800.

items.title: No family ties between five students and VIPs or politicians, Zara inquest told
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Police found no family ties between Students A, B, C, D and E and any VIPs, VVIPs or politicians, the Coroner's Court was told. Investigating officer Inspector Wong Yew Zhung also testified that his investigation found no evidence of protection, influence or other intervention by VIPs, VVIPs or politicians to help the students evade legal action. Fikry: Based on your investigation, did you find that any VIPs, VVIPs or politicians had family ties with Students A, B, C, D and E?

items.title: [UPDATED] Nazir Hussin refuses MACC asset declaration notice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin has refused to accept an asset declaration notice issued by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). Nazir, his wife and an assistant were summoned to MACC headquarters in Putrajaya today to assist in the investigation. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Nazir was called in to receive a notice requiring him to declare his assets under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: RTD Ops Luxury: The price of looking rich
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Cheah, 36, bought a second-hand BMW X6 for RM40,000, hoping the luxury badge would help him project success and win people's trust. He admitted that he and some of his peers had underestimated the cost of ownership, particularly insurance and road tax. Cheah said the Transport Ministry's decision to allow private vehicle owners to use digital road tax instead of displaying a physical disc had made things easier, particularly during enforcement operations.

items.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have worsened sharply in recent months. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defence capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security.

items.title: Epicon unit secures RM47.38mil subcontract for NPE extension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Epicon Bhd's 70 per cent-owned subsidiary, Concrete Empire Sdn Bhd (CESB), has secured a RM47.38 million subcontract for the supply of precast segmental crossheads for the privatisation project of the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) Extension. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Epicon said CESB had accepted a letter of acceptance from IJM Corporation Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, IJM Construction Sdn Bhd. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: AWC unit bags RM39.70mil subcontract for hyperscale data centre
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AWC Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, Qudotech Sdn Bhd, has entered into a subcontract agreement with Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd involving a hyperscale data centre project worth RM39.70 million in Bandar Spring Hill, Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, AWC said the agreement entails the construction and completion of a cold-water system, rainwater harvesting system, water reticulation system, fire hydrant system and sanitary service, among others. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MCE secures RM23mil supply contracts from US-based client
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCE Holdings Bhd has secured new contracts worth approximately RM23.29 million to supply automotive electronic components to a US-based automotive components supplier for the US market. The contracts, awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Multi-Code Electronics Industries (M) Bhd, involve the supply of automotive electronic components, including display electronic control units, for a US vehicle programme over a period of 60 months. MCE is a Malaysian Tier-1 automotive supplier specialising in the design, engineering and manufacturing of automotive electronics and mechatronic components, with a global footprint spanning Japan, India and exports spanning Asia, the Americas, the Middle East and Australia.

items.title: Police: BYD driver to be charged over fatal Jalan Kuching crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle collision that killed a five-year-old girl on Jalan Kuching is to be charged at the Magistrates Court tomorrow. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the investigation team arrested the 24-year-old suspect immediately after he was discharged from a private hospital, where he had sought treatment. Mohd Zamzuri said the suspect would be charged under Sections 41(1), 42(1) and 52(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by dangerous or reckless driving, dangerous or reckless driving, and failing to stop after an accident, respectively.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Customs cannot be defended by breaching the rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir today said customs cannot be defended by breaking the very rules of custom, in a pointed address directed at those who have disputed the rules of succession in recent months. Speaking at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this afternoon to mark the investiture of the 17th Undang of Luak Jelebu, Tuanku Muhriz said Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional monarchy, adat and legal provisions must be upheld together. Disputes must follow custom and law The Yamtuan further said the customary system must continue to be strengthened to remain relevant with the times, without neglecting its founding principles and rules.

items.title: Public Services Commission awaits circular on RM2,500 starting salary for fresh grads entering public service
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 14 — The implementation of the RM2,500 starting salary for fresh graduates entering the public service, announced in Budget 2027, is pending an official circular outlining the implementation details. Malaysian Public Services Commission (SPA) chairman and Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the details would include the implementation timeline and related payment components. Asked whether the RM2,500 amount included other allowances, Ahmad Jailani said the matter would be reviewed and clarified in the official circular.

items.title: Malaysia gives Nepal US$1m in flood relief aid
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan presented the contribution to Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur, Mudita Bajracharya, at a ceremony here on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra. “The contribution reflects Malaysia’s unwavering support for the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” Wisma Putra said in a statement. “The new ordinance will provide greater legal and administrative certainty for affected families,” Wisma Putra said.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang will reopen tomorrow. The Selangor State Education Department said school operations in the state will prioritise the safety, health and well-being of pupils and school staff. The Melaka State Education Department said educational institutions under MOE will resume operations tomorrow, pending official confirmation of the latest API readings.

items.title: Parliament’s new service council to be fully operational by December, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker
items.summary: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the council would oversee matters including the service scheme, career paths and administration of parliamentary officers, as well as ensure compliance with the provisions of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025. The event was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The four appointees, comprising two government and two opposition representatives, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu).

items.title: Weather warning: MetMalaysia puts most of the country on thunderstorm alert
items.summary: Perak faces widespread disruption across Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, and Bagan Datuk. Across Selangor, the warning blankets Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, and Sepang. Across East Malaysia, the warning stretches across multiple divisions in Sarawak.

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial: Prosecution cites contradictions in four accused’s defence
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 14 — The High Court here was told today that there are four main grounds for the prosecution’s bid to convict the four accused in the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago, with the contention that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week. “The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now.

items.title: Five govt buildings get solar installations ahead of schedule, says works minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Five grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) solar installation projects at government buildings have been completed ahead of schedule, with a combined installed capacity of 779.86 kilowatts, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said. He said the Public Works Department (JKR) had also implemented grid-connected photovoltaic and off-grid solar installations involving 46 Federal Government buildings, 283 rural schools in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, four Royal Malaysia Police border posts and an Orang Asli village. As of last September, eight projects involving 23 buildings with a capacity of 5.8 megawatts had completed their Defects Liability Period (DLP), while seven projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 2.09 megawatts remained within the period.

items.title: Sarawak Education Dept: Schools open tomorrow, outdoor activities halted if API tops 100
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 14 — All schools and educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Sarawak will operate as usual tomorrow, despite the ongoing haze affecting several areas in the state. In a statement today, the Sarawak Education Department (JPN) said schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 100 must suspend all outdoor activities. “Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure amid the current haze situation.

items.title: Why should a good man go when the corrupt stay? Anwar says Malaysia needs ministers like Anthony Loke
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim sought again today to make a case for Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to remain in his Cabinet, saying the country needs principled leaders and that the corrupt should be the ones stepping down. Speaking at the Transport Ministry during the distribution of RM1,000 special financial assistance to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers, Anwar commended Loke's dedication to ordinary working Malaysians, including the initiative today. Loke, who is the DAP secretary-general, tendered his resignation as transport minister on September 19 following the political controversy surrounding the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

items.title: MACC: Fighting corruption starts with rejecting bribes, reporting misconduct
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Chief Commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman said building a corruption-free culture starts with honest decisions and firm personal convictions, supported by sustained commitment from all parties. He was speaking at the launch of the “Program Langkah Merdeka 118, Bersama Perangi Rasuah” programme, held in conjunction with the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration for Kuala Lumpur at Stadium Merdeka here today. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib said the symbolic act of carrying and hoisting the MACC flag atop Merdeka 118, Malaysia’s tallest building and the world’s second tallest, reflected the commission’s determination to elevate the anti-corruption agenda and strengthen integrity without compromise.

items.title: Paddy farmers who suffered yield losses from fertiliser delays may get targeted aid, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government will assess whether to provide targeted assistance to paddy farmers whose yields declined due to delays in fertiliser supplies, evaluating affected cases on a case-by-case basis. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the assessment would identify farmers who genuinely suffered losses before considering any assistance. In a separate development, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said 10 per cent of the funds collected through the Warriors’ Fund Campaign (KTP) had been allocated for investment in fixed deposits with financial institutions.

items.title: Foreign minister: Malaysians in Riyadh, Jeddah safe amid Saudi tensions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysians living and working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have been reported safe amid continuing tensions in the country, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah confirmed that Malaysians in both cities were safe and well. He said the security situation in Saudi Arabia remained tense following another reported attack yesterday.

items.title: Johor JPJ seeks p-hailing operators’ help to curb repeat offences, especially running red lights
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 14 — The Johor Road Transport Department (JPJ) will meet p-hailing operators to discuss measures to raise riders’ awareness of road safety and curb repeat traffic offences, particularly running red lights. State JPJ director Zulkarnain Yasin said the department had received numerous complaints about traffic offences involving p-hailing riders, particularly running red lights, captured in dashboard camera footage. He said JPJ also imposed demerit points on road users who repeatedly committed offences such as running red lights, in addition to issuing summonses.

items.title: Budget 2027: Tengku Zafrul urges local semiconductor firms to move up value chain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Local semiconductor companies must translate Budget 2027’s allocation into greater participation in higher-value activities such as integrated circuit (IC) design, as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its position in the global semiconductor supply chain, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Speaking on Bernama TV’s The Nation programme, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman said Malaysia has developed a mature semiconductor ecosystem over more than five decades but needs to move beyond its traditional strengths in assembly and testing to capture greater value from the industry. Tengku Zafrul said the measures would help Malaysian companies strengthen their capabilities and move further up the value chain.

items.title: 1MDB trial: Judge rejects Najib’s bid to stay prison sentence, says his medical issues not special circumstances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The High Court today dismissed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) corruption case. Delivering her decision, High Court Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin held that the gravity of the offences and overarching public interest considerations outweighed the applicant's private grievances. “Having weighed the competing interests of the applicant against public interest considerations, the court does not agree that the medical issues raised satisfy the special circumstances test,” the judge said.

items.title: Damansara mini tornado caused by active thunderstorm clouds, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The mini tornado or landspout that struck Damansara, Selangor, yesterday evening was caused by active thunderstorm clouds (cumulonimbus), said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. Mohd Hisham said tornadoes in Malaysia occur only on a relatively small scale, measuring less than 10 metres and lasting for a very short time. Mohd Hisham said landspouts, tornadoes over land and waterspouts over the sea occur frequently during the monsoon transition phase, from March to May and September to October.

items.title: Man drives SUV 130m down train tracks in Port Klang, police say KTMB investigating
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 14 — A 60-year-old motorist drove his SUV onto railway tracks and travelled roughly 130 metres before coming to a stop at a KTMB station in Pelabuhan Klang, police confirmed today. The late-night incident occurred around 11.40pm on Oct 11 at a level crossing near the Jalan Limbungan KTMB station, Klang South district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said in a statement today. “According to preliminary police investigations, the driver, a Kuala Lumpur resident, was heading home when his vehicle strayed onto the tracks,” Lim said.

items.title: King attends 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara, chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. Present were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim, also attended.

items.title: Anwar hails Parliamentary Services Act as key reform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 as a key step by the MADANI Government towards fulfilling its reform pledge to the people, including limiting powers traditionally held by the government. He said the move was a key pillar of the country’s reform agenda, reflecting the government’s commitment to strengthening Parliament’s independence and advancing the maturity of the country’s parliamentary democracy. “I consider this change and the Parliamentary Services Act important because they give meaning to parliamentary democracy and reflect the maturity of our democratic system.

items.title: MPS urges Putrajaya to detail contract pharmacists’ absorption timeline and quota numbers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) has welcomed the government’s move to recommend contract pharmacy officers for permanent posts, but insists Putrajaya must quickly settle the critical details on quota figures, eligibility rules, and an implementation timeline. The response follows remarks by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, who confirmed on Monday that the Ministry of Health (MOH) will submit a proposal to the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet to absorb contract pharmacy officers into permanent positions. He said permanent posts for dental and pharmacy personnel will come from a distinct allocation, separate from the 9,000 permanent medical officer positions unveiled under Budget 2027.
